name: shift-enter-newline
opens_with: Composer has text and the operator reaches for the newline chord
notes: The operator's 2026-11-02 report: 'SHIFT+ENTER like utility typing shortcuts are not working'. The production key handler was never the gap — Enter+SHIFT has mapped to `insert_newline` since iter-120 and has a passing unit test. The gap was in the HARNESS: `parse_generic_chord` (cmd_tui_debug.rs) required exactly one character after the `+`, so `<shift+enter>` fell through to None and `parse_key_sequence` typed the whole token as its literal characters — eleven keystrokes of `shift+enter` into the composer. No scenario could exercise the chord, so the report could be neither reproduced nor ruled out from the corpus. Fixed by `chord_key_code`, which names the non-character keys. This scenario is the durable pin: the `not-contains:shift+enter` assertion is the whole point — if the parser regresses to literal typing, the eleven characters appear on screen and this scenario goes red. Params `not-contains:shift` would also fail on a trailing space; the full token is asserted so a partial regression still trips it. "messages == 0" pins that the chord inserted rather than submitted.
